items.title: Allen Toussaint Interview, 1979-03-13
items.q: Well, in a way the same for Irma Thomas, but there are some songs that I wrote for Irma that sound quite normal to me as a normal song.

ctx.x: You had to leave minute records for the Army. What happened? Were you drafted in 1963?

Right. That must have really disrupted things. A bit, yes. I was, by that time I was ready to go to the Army. I had been deferred a couple of times before then. And one time I was out because my left foot was in a cast from putting on trampoline shows. I had an accident. But I had been deferred a couple of times. So by January of 63, I didn't mind going to Army. A lot of artists did leave and ventured to other places. Of course, it was a blessing for some, seemingly. The first actual million seller that Irma had…
And you just heard it on the radio while you were probably on the case.

items.title: Allen Toussaint Interview, 1979-03-13
items.q: So when It's Rainin' was written, I'ma was there. For most of the songs she was right there, actually.

ctx.x: Okay. At that time, it seemed like almost all the New Orleans music that we know today was being written by you like It's Raining and Ruler of My Heart and Over You. Did you write those songs specifically with, okay, did you write It's Raining with Irma Thomas in mind or did she come to you and say, connect me up with something that I'll be able to sing well? How did that go? How did that go?

and songs like It's Rainin' the Root of My Heart, the artist was usually right there, and we'd write one tune, and sing it down once and the artist go, and in the next room in practice while we write another song for someone else. Then one come out of the other room, and we'd sing that, and then the other one would go in the other room. And whoever wasn't working on their own songs would sing background for the others. So when It's Rainin' was written, I'ma was there. For most of the songs she was right there,…
on the way between parts. So music just comes to you at all different times of the day, and it's something that never stops.
